script: Posting Podcasts, Surveys, or your college homework will get you banned.. I was deleting a post every two days, like a cleaning crew on a haunted house tour. My inbox was a black hole of "check this out" messages that looked like spam from the 90s. Then I thought, "I need a sticky post to set the record straight." But here's the thing… I am not here to waste your time with boring guidelines. I am here to drop the tea on the three things that will get you banned faster than a meme on a no‑filter account. Podcast‑ers, listen up. If you're scraping through the depths of a subreddit just to find content, that's a sign your channel with 586 subs probably won't explode. (Seriously, you can't even carry a show by yourself, so what's the point?) The audacity of trying to monetize a dumpster fire? That's a red flag, bestie. And that's when everything changed… Survey creators, you're on a collision course. 95% of our users aren't hotel employees, so your survey data is a statistical black hole. It's like throwing a snowball at a mirror and hoping it turns into a diamond. (What I didn't know was how quickly people start calling you out for "fake" data.) The stakes? You lose credibility before the first click. College students, this one's for you. Your professor will be like, "Where did you get that source?" if you include a Reddit thread asking every question they could think of. Unless you're faking citations or your college is okay with a "sourceless" essay (which is a whole different drama), you're signing up for a grade of "I need more work." If this didn't work, I'd lose everything – my GPA, my sanity, my ability to binge watch my own shows. The emotional cost? I couldn't eat, I couldn't sleep. But here's the thing… you can always try r/askhotels, but they're probably as tired of it as we are. Imagine a room full of people whispering "this is fine" while the floor cracks under their feet. That's what the subreddit feels like when you keep dropping the same content. And that's when everything changed… So, I am dropping this sticky because I am better than the people who keep posting the same old nonsense. I've seen it all – the loop of reposting, the disappointment of low engagement, the fear of losing your account. I am the voice that says, "Stop, breathe, and think before you hit submit." What I didn't know was that some of you were so desperate for validation they'd post anything, even if it was a Reddit thread masquerading as research. The stakes? Your reputation. Your future. Your sanity. I know, right? (Literally insane how many people still think a meme can be a citation.) The tension is real, the wave is building. I've got my eyes on the horizon, and the only thing I want is for you to stop the cycle. If you're still thinking, "Can I just do it anyway?" let me break it down: every post you delete is a step toward a cleaner, stronger brand. Every sticky you ignore is a missed chance to show the world you've got the best content. So, what happened next? I posted the sticky. I got a few comments, a few likes, and a handful of people finally realizing they were on the wrong track. That's the part nobody saw coming. And that's the final tea: keep it original, keep it legit, and keep your account safe. If you're still unsure, remember the stakes are high and the consequences are permanent. Stay woke, bestie, and let's keep it real.
